Nigeria gained independence from Britain on 1st October 1960.
Nigeria became a republic in 1963.
Abuja became Nigeria's capital city in 1991, replacing Lagos.
Nigeria has 36 states and one Federal Capital Territory.
Nigeria's National Assembly has two chambers: the Senate and the House of Representatives.
The Nigerian Senate has 109 members.
The House of Representatives has 360 members.
A Nigerian president serves a four-year term.
A person can only be elected president twice in Nigeria.
Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe was Nigeria's first ceremonial president.
Shehu Shagari was Nigeria's first executive president.
Abubakar Tafawa Balewa was Nigeria's first prime minister.
Nigeria experienced its first military coup in January 1966.
Nigeria returned to democratic rule on 29th May 1999.
Olusegun Obasanjo was Nigeria's first elected president under the Fourth Republic.
Nigeria has three arms of government: Executive, Legislature and Judiciary.
Herbert Macaulay is widely regarded as the father of Nigerian nationalism.
Nigeria's first political party was the Nigerian National Democratic Party (NNDP), founded in 1923.
Patricia Etteh became Nigeria's first female Speaker of the House of Representatives in 2007.
Nigeria's president lives and works at the Presidential Villa in Abuja.
